Subject: FinLedger post-call: SLO / parallel request & connection-thread follow-up

Hi Ellen / Adam — thanks again for the call this morning. Rapid recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance requirements and a path for quota/limit conversations.

Key requirements you mentioned on the call:
- Latency: p50 ~30ms, p95 < 70ms for non-streaming token completion; streaming UI p95 chunk latency target ~80–120ms.
- Throughput: steady-state ~600 reqs/min during peak (10 reqs/sec sustained), with spikes up to 250 reqs/min for short bursts.
- Concurrency: your frontend will open parallel conversational sessions — you expect up to 120 concurrent live sessions with 1–2 active generation requests per session, so we should plan for ~180 parallel in-flight generation requests at peak.
- Connection pooling: long-lived connections from our edge (keepalive) with streaming over HTTP/2 or WebSocket preferred.

What I took away from the Redwood side that matters for quota discussion:
- Default hosted account concurrency is 30 parallel requests, with standard rate limits set conservatively for new accounts.
- We can provision a dedicated concurrency bump (reserved burst tokens) or a scoped per-route concurrency increase after a short attestation and runbook.
- Streaming has slightly different resource accounting because of chunked responses and open connections; we typically recommend capping number of open streams per client and using auto-shard + prefix cache for frequent prompts.

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm):
1) FinLedger to confirm whether 180 parallel in-flight requests is the peak we should provision for, or if 120 is a safer planning number.
2) I’ll put together a short SLO table (latency/availability) and a mutual action plan doc to formalize the timing for a provisional concurrency bump to 150 and a further increase to 250 if the early load test looks good.
3) We’ll need a short security checklist + contact for the procurement team so our ops can authorize the temporary quota change.

Attaching the mutual action plan draft and a template SLO spreadsheet. If you’re ok, I’ll loop in Marissa to approve the provisional increase and Lauren to schedule a short load-test window next week.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinLedger post-call: SLO / parallel request & connection-thread follow-up

Thanks Jonas — quick clarifications:
- The 120 concurrent sessions comment maps to our product MAU model; the 180 number is conservative if every session triggers parallel calls (UI + background sync). For planning, please assume 180 in-flight generators at peak.
- For streaming, our client will hold a single streaming connection per active session (so up to 120 open streams); the extra parallelism comes from background batch/rerank calls.
- We can provide a procurement contact (procurement@finledger.com) and our security lead (Adam) will share the SOC2 scoping questions today.

Can Redwood provision a provisional concurrency bump to 150 today so we can run a smoke test and then move to 250 if the load test results look good? Also need to know expected cost delta / pricing for that provisional capacity.

—Ellen

Ellen — thanks for the fast reply and for sending procurement contact. Quick answers and what we can do today: 

1) Concurrency bump: we can approve a provisional increase to 150 parallel in-flight generation requests for a 72-hour smoke window while we run your test harness. If smoke is clean, we’ll accelerate a second-tier increase to 250 (requires brief attestation + billing commit).
2) Streaming behavior: we will count open streaming connections separately from CPU token accounting; by default we allow up to 100 open streams per account — for FinLedger we can raise that to 140 for the smoke window to match your 120 active streams plus headroom.
3) Pricing: provisional capacity bumps are billed at a short-term uplift (approx +35% over base hosted token rates) for provisional reserved concurrency; sustained increases convert to reserved capacity pricing (lower per-unit). I’ll share a short pricing note separately.
4) Operational controls: we’ll enable per-route concurrency caps and a routing fallback to a lower-cost model in case of sustained overload. We’ll also provide a temporary quota token (opportunity_id FL-2026-0421-proxy) that your ops team can reference when we open the bump.

Attaching the updated SLO table (latency buckets and targets) and the mutual action plan with timeline. Can Marissa approve the bump and Lauren coordinate a Wednesday load window (UTC-friendly)?

Thanks — Jonas
